item.title: Alberto G. Valerio
item.description:
Alberto G. Valerio is a Ph.D. Student at the Computational Intelligence Laboratory (CILab), University of Bari Aldo Moro. His research focuses on Artificial Intelligence for healthcare, with particular emphasis on medical imaging and Explainable Artificial Intelligence.

His work investigates deep-learning and graph-based methods for analysing biomedical data, including brain imaging and neurological diseases, together with methodologies for evaluating and interpreting model explanations.

A further direction concerns the integration of Large Language Models and structured biomedical information to support more interpretable and informative AI-assisted analysis.

item.title: Ciro Castiello
item.description:
Ciro Castiello is an Associate Professor at the Department of Computer Science, University of Bari Aldo Moro. His research focuses on fuzzy systems, soft computing and inductive learning, with particular attention to the construction of models whose behaviour can be interpreted and critically assessed.

A central theme of his research is the relationship between predictive capability and interpretability, connecting traditional fuzzy modelling with contemporary Explainable Artificial Intelligence.

He has participated in several research projects and is active in national and international scientific communities in fuzzy systems, soft computing and Computational Intelligence.

item.title: Corrado Mencar
item.description:
Corrado Mencar is an Associate Professor in Computer Science at the University of Bari Aldo Moro. His research focuses on Granular Computing, fuzzy systems and intelligent data analysis, with particular attention to interpretable representations of complex information.

His work investigates fuzzy and granular models, information granulation and interpretable machine-learning approaches, contributing to the broader development of Explainable Artificial Intelligence from a Computational Intelligence perspective.

He is active in scientific societies and international initiatives related to fuzzy systems, granular computing and explainable AI.

item.title: Davide Cazzorla
item.description:
Davide Cazzorla is a Ph.D. Student at the Computational Intelligence Laboratory (CILab), University of Bari Aldo Moro. His research focuses on Explainable Artificial Intelligence and uncertainty-aware machine learning.

His work investigates probabilistic and fuzzy approaches for representing uncertainty, including fuzzy clustering and interpretable decision-support models.

These methods are also studied in the context of AI-supported procurement and decision-making, where transparency, uncertainty and the explicit representation of evaluation criteria play a central role.

item.title: Emanuele Colonna
item.description:
Emanuele Colonna is a Contract Researcher at the Computational Intelligence Laboratory (CILab), University of Bari Aldo Moro. His research focuses on Computer Vision and Deep Learning, with particular interest in generative and multimodal models.

His work investigates vision-language learning, generative approaches and representations that connect visual information with natural language and other modalities.

A major application direction concerns Sign Language understanding and translation, where multimodal AI can support the modelling of complex relationships between visual gestures and linguistic information.

item.title: Emanuele Fontana
item.description:
Emanuele Fontana is a Ph.D. Student at the Computational Intelligence Laboratory (CILab), University of Bari Aldo Moro. His research focuses on trustworthy foundation models and mechanistic interpretability, with particular emphasis on the real-time detection and mitigation of hallucinations in Large Language Models.

His work investigates latent-space alignment and shared representations across different model architectures, with the goal of identifying transferable truthfulness features and developing lightweight detection and steering mechanisms that do not require model-specific retraining, external retrieval systems, or multiple inference passes.

item.title: Gabriella Casalino
item.description:
Gabriella Casalino is a Tenure-Track Assistant Professor at the Department of Computer Science, University of Bari Aldo Moro. Her research lies in Computational Intelligence and intelligent data analysis, with particular emphasis on eHealth, evolving data, fuzzy modelling and Explainable Artificial Intelligence.

Her work investigates methods for analysing heterogeneous and dynamic data, including data streams, images, physiological signals and clinical information. Healthcare is a major application domain, where interpretability and the ability to adapt to complex data distributions are especially important.

item.title: Gennaro Vessio
item.description:
Gennaro Vessio is an Associate Professor at the Department of Computer Science, University of Bari Aldo Moro. His research focuses on Deep Learning and Computer Vision, with growing emphasis on multimodal, efficient and trustworthy Artificial Intelligence.

His work investigates visual and multimodal representations, generative and knowledge-aware models, explainability, and resource-efficient learning. A recurring objective is to develop AI methods that can move beyond controlled benchmarks and operate under the constraints of real-world systems.

item.title: Giovanna Castellano
item.description:
Giovanna Castellano is a Full Professor at the Department of Computer Science, University of Bari Aldo Moro, where she coordinates the Computational Intelligence Laboratory (CILab). Her research spans Computational Intelligence, Computer Vision and Deep Learning, with a long-standing interest in fuzzy systems, interpretable models and Explainable Artificial Intelligence.

Her work combines methodological research with applications to complex domains, including healthcare, visual data analysis and intelligent decision-support systems.

She coordinates the Ph.D. program in Computer Science at the University of Bari Aldo Moro and has led research activities in national projects, including NEED — Next-Gen Digital Diagnostics: Bridging AI Explainability and Medical Trust and FAIR — Future Artificial Intelligence Research, where she was PI of WP6.4 on the understandability of AI systems.

item.title: Ivan Rinaldi
item.description:
Ivan Rinaldi is a Ph.D. Student at the Computational Intelligence Laboratory (CILab), University of Bari Aldo Moro. His research focuses on Multimodal Artificial Intelligence and generative models, with particular attention to learning relationships across different forms of information.

His work investigates audio-visual and vision-language learning, including methods that connect images, video, language and sound within shared or coordinated representations.

item.title: Lorenzo Abatescianni
item.description:
Lorenzo Abatescianni is a Ph.D. Student at the Computational Intelligence Laboratory (CILab), University of Bari Aldo Moro. His research focuses on knowledge-driven and neuro-symbolic Artificial Intelligence for safety-critical systems, with particular emphasis on railway applications.

His work investigates the integration of formal ontologies and Railway Knowledge Graphs with deep-learning architectures, including Graph Neural Networks and temporal graph models, to incorporate structural and domain knowledge into data-driven representations.

A major objective is to develop interpretable-by-design AI models for railway systems, with applications to signaling anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, and intelligent decision support, combining predictive capabilities with domain constraints and regulatory knowledge.

item.title: Lucrezia Laraspata
item.description:
Lucrezia Laraspata is a Ph.D. Student at the Computational Intelligence Laboratory (CILab), University of Bari Aldo Moro. Her research focuses on Large Language Models and Trustworthy AI, with particular emphasis on mechanistic interpretability and the analysis of internal model representations.

Her work investigates how information related to truthfulness and hallucinations is encoded in the latent representations of Large Language Models, exploring probing and representation engineering techniques to better understand and control model behavior.

item.title: Maria Creanza
item.description:
Maria Creanza is a Ph.D. Student at the Computational Intelligence Laboratory (CILab), University of Bari Aldo Moro. Her research focuses on Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence for Digital Mental Health, with particular emphasis on continuous monitoring from heterogeneous physiological, behavioural, acoustic, and contextual data.

Her work investigates learning under limited labelled data and multimodal learning, exploring self-supervised, semi-supervised and transfer learning approaches, foundation models, and different strategies for integrating multiple data modalities.

item.title: Pasquale De Marinis
item.description:
Pasquale De Marinis is a Postdoctoral Researcher at the Computational Intelligence Laboratory (CILab), University of Bari Aldo Moro. His research focuses on Computer Vision and Deep Learning, with particular attention to learning effectively from limited data and computational resources.

His work includes few-shot learning and semantic segmentation, efficient deep-learning architectures and adaptation strategies, and methods for understanding and explaining the behaviour of modern vision models.

A further research direction concerns the deployment of visual intelligence in real-world and resource-constrained settings, including drone-based and edge AI applications.

item.title: Raffaele Scaringi
item.description:
Raffaele Scaringi is a Postdoctoral Researcher at the Computational Intelligence Laboratory (CILab), University of Bari Aldo Moro. His research lies at the intersection of Computer Vision, Deep Learning and structured knowledge representation.

His work investigates graph-based and knowledge-aware approaches for enriching visual representations with semantic and contextual information, including the integration of knowledge graphs and visual data.

A major application area is cultural heritage and digital humanities, where these methods support the analysis, organization and interpretation of visual art collections.

item.title: Walter Mangione
item.description:
Walter Mangione is a Ph.D. Student at the Computational Intelligence Laboratory (CILab), University of Bari Aldo Moro. His research focuses on Artificial Intelligence for the study of brain diseases, combining graph-based learning with Explainable Artificial Intelligence.

His work investigates brain connectomes as graph-structured data and the use of Graph Neural Networks for analysing relationships between brain connectivity patterns and neurological or neurodegenerative conditions.

A central objective is to develop models whose predictions can be interpreted in terms of relevant brain structures and connections, linking graph learning, medical AI and explainability.
